title: A core's status change writes its own Part History entry
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-COREHIST-01), with description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL COREHIST PART), is tracked at {Location-A} with a Core Charge (for example $25.00), so it has a core, {Core-A}, described "Core for {Description-A}".
  • {Part-A} and {Core-A} are active.
  • You know how to open {Core-A}'s own Part History page, which names the core "Core for {Description-A}".
custom_steps:
1. On the Active tab search {Part-A}, click its row, pick Part Status "Inactive", click Save, type the note "ZZAUTOTEST core follows" and click "Deactivate" in the "Deactivate part?" confirmation.
  2. Open {Core-A}'s own Part History page.
  3. Read the newest entry.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Part-A} moves to the Inactive tab.
  • Step 2: The page is the core's own: its part details name it "Core for {Description-A}".
  • Step 3: The newest entry is the core's own "Deactivated | Reason: ZZAUTOTEST core follows".

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S10-R19, S2-R17, S5-E3, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas 13 Oct copy: no board shows a core. Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan", 7 Oct 2026 (informs, never overrules), §6 Phase 2 tests. Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6): a core has no row of its own; its history shows on the core's own Part History page. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R19: “A core's status change writes its own Part History entry on the core.”
  • S2-R17: “A part's core becomes inactive together with the part, in the same change.”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • Tech plan (Parts Lifecycle Update, 7 Oct 2026), §6 Phase 2 tests: “one `entity_event` per parent + core with the note”
